body:
This requirement currently says this:


| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **14.1.2** | Verify that compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found. | | ✓ | ✓ | 120 |

It was formed from the merging of two other requirements:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| **[19.9](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blame/6c146ac7f48abb32ce979c6a10a451168cb1068e/4.0/en/0x24-V19-Config.md#L23)** | Verify that build processes for system level languages have all security flags enabled, such as ASLR, DEP, and security checks.  |  |  | ✓ |  |
| **[5.3.13](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blame/fc7af2668e4c957c2eb42b196d1afad72e1bf2b1/4.0/en/0x13-V5-Input-Validation.md)** | Verify that if the application uses a systems language or unmanaged code, compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found. |  |  | ✓ |  |

My question would be, can we think of ways to make this more general to relate to securely compiling other languages as well rather than just handling c/c++ memory issues?

comments.body: Some time from opening the issue and maybe we have different understanding of the scope for v5.0 - are you sure the requirement is in the scope for ASVS v5.0?

> **[5.3.13](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/blame/fc7af2668e4c957c2eb42b196d1afad72e1bf2b1/4.0/en/0x13-V5-Input-Validation.md)**	Verify that if the application uses a systems language or unmanaged code, compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found.			✓	

Quick curious question @tghosth: what does this "unmanaged code" part means? I had a hard time understanding this requirement whenever I read it due to that part.

> what does this "unmanaged code" part means? I 

So I think Java, C#, Javascript, etc, would be considered managed code because they have the JVM/.NET framework that handles low level concerns like memory allocation

C and C++ would be be considered unmanaged because they do not.

> Are you sure the requirement is in the scope for ASVS v5.0?

I think this is borderline. I would be inclined to keep in scope because it is more connected to preparation of the application than the surrounding processes. For example:

* Here we excluded something mostly because it was not relevant for a web app and also because it was about the deploy of the application, not the preparation of the application:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1530

* Here we excluded something because it was also about the deploy of the application, not the preparation of the application:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1245

* Here we excluded something because it was about the security of the pipeline, not the application:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1566

* Here we excluded somethings because they were more like processes than a control in the application:
https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/1467

I accept that 14.1.2 seems a little like a process but I think practically speaking it is getting the compiler to add security controls into the application and therefore I think it should be in scope.
Can't think of anything so I am going to close this for now.

I think 13.4.4 can go.

_13.4.4 Verify that compiler flags are configured to enable all available buffer overflow protections and warnings, including stack randomization, data execution prevention, and to break the build if an unsafe pointer, memory, format string, integer, or string operations are found._

This does not at all necessarily lead to a vulnerability especially if you are using SAST and other tools outside of compile time. This is also not testable in production. 

Since it's not a real risk, I think it should go.

I think there is good support for removing this (including from #2280) but I would like to clarify the use of the compiler flags in related requirements.

Opened #3002
I think moving this to section text was the right move. Thank you.
